dish.name: Dindigul Chicken Biryani
dish.description: A famous Tamil Nadu style chicken biryani made with fragrant short-grain Seeraga Samba rice, shallow-fried shallots, fresh green chillies, and tender chicken cooked together in a spiced meat broth.

Mortar and pestle or small grinder

steps.title: Prepare shallots and chilli base
steps.text: Finely chop 60g shallots and crush 10g green chillies using a mortar and pestle into a coarse paste.
steps.visualCue: Shallots are diced finely and chillies form a coarse, pungent green paste.
steps.watchOut: Do not blend chillies into a watery purée; coarse pounding gives authentic Dindigul flavor and texture. Juice splashing into eyes is a common hazard when pounding chillies. cameraCheck: Chopped shallots and crushed green chilli paste side-by-side on cutting board. Video shot: Top-down shot of pounding chillies in a mortar. Tip: Wear gloves or wash hands thoroughly after handling green chillies.

steps.title: Heat oil and ghee
steps.text: Place a pressure cooker on medium flame and add 10ml vegetable oil along with 10ml ghee.
steps.visualCue: Ghee melts completely and oil shimmers gently without smoking.
steps.watchOut: Do not overheat fat to smoking point, which burns whole spices immediately upon adding. cameraCheck: Shimmering melted ghee and oil mixture in cooker bottom. Video shot: Pouring ghee into hot oil inside the pressure cooker.

steps.title: Sauté whole spices
steps.text: Add 3g whole spices (cloves, cardamom, cinnamon, star anise) to the hot fat and cook for 30 seconds.
steps.visualCue: Whole spices sizzle immediately, swell up slightly, and release a warm aromatic fragrance.
steps.watchOut: If spices turn dark brown or black within seconds, the oil is too hot; lower flame immediately. cameraCheck: Sizzling spices dancing in hot ghee oil. Video shot: Close-up of spices sizzle in oil. Timer: 30 seconds.

steps.title: Sauté chopped shallots
steps.text: Add 60g chopped shallots into the cooker and sauté on medium heat for 4 minutes until light golden.
steps.visualCue: Shallots turn translucent, soft, and take on a light golden color along edges.
steps.watchOut: Do not dark-brown the shallots like Hyderabadi biryani onions, or the broth color and flavor profile will become bitter. cameraCheck: Translucent golden-tinged shallots in cooker. Video shot: Medium shot of wooden spatula stirring shallots in cooker. Timer: 240 seconds.

steps.title: Add green chilli and ginger-garlic paste
steps.text: Add 10g crushed green chilli paste and 15g ginger-garlic paste, cooking for 2 minutes while stirring continuously.
steps.visualCue: Raw sharp aroma disappears and oil begins to separate slightly from the aromatic paste.
steps.watchOut: Ginger-garlic paste sticks quickly to the bottom; scrape continuously with spatula. cameraCheck: Paste mixed into shallots with subtle oil bubbles around edges. Video shot: Close-up of spatula stirring thick paste. Timer: 120 seconds.

steps.title: Add herbs, curd, and seasoning
steps.text: Add 10g mint leaves, 10g coriander, 40g curd, 4g salt, and 5ml lemon juice. Stir well for 2 minutes on low heat.
steps.visualCue: Curd melts smoothly into a green-tinted thick gravy base without curdling.
steps.watchOut: Adding curd on high heat causes separation into watery curds; lower flame before adding. cameraCheck: Creamy spiced herb gravy simmering gently. Video shot: Curd and herbs being folded into spice base. Timer: 120 seconds.

steps.title: Sear chicken in the spice base
steps.text: Add 180g chicken pieces into the cooker gravy and sauté on medium-high heat for 5 minutes until chicken turns opaque outside.
steps.visualCue: Chicken surface changes from pink to opaque white, coated thoroughly in gravy.
steps.watchOut: Ensure heat is high enough to sear meat so juices lock in before liquid is added. cameraCheck: Opaque chicken pieces thoroughly coated in thick gravy. Video shot: Flipping chicken pieces in the hot curry base. Timer: 300 seconds.

steps.title: Add water and bring meat broth to a boil
steps.text: Pour 175ml water into the cooker, mix thoroughly, cover loosely, and bring to a rapid rolling boil for 4 minutes.
steps.visualCue: Steam vents vigorously and liquid bubbles rapidly with oil floating on top.
steps.watchOut: Measure water precisely; excess water will result in soggy porridge-like Seeraga Samba rice. cameraCheck: Rapidly boiling reddish-brown chicken broth. Video shot: Pouring water into cooker and stirring broth. Timer: 240 seconds.

steps.title: Stir in drained rice and cover for dum
steps.text: Drain soaked rice completely, gently stir into boiling broth, close cooker lid tightly with weight on, and cook on lowest flame for 10 minutes.
steps.visualCue: Steam seals inside cooker and faint aroma of spice-infused rice escaping weight.
steps.watchOut: Do not cook on high flame or rice will burn at the bottom before cooking through; keep flame at absolute minimum. cameraCheck: Rice stirred into broth right before lid is closed. Video shot: Adding drained rice to boiling broth and placing cooker lid. Timer: 600 seconds.

steps.title: Rest before opening
steps.text: Turn off flame completely and allow cooker to rest untouched for 10 minutes to finish cooking on trapped steam.
steps.visualCue: Pressure drops naturally and no steam releases when weight is lifted gently.
steps.watchOut: Opening immediately will make rice grains collapse into a sticky mass; resting lets moisture distribute evenly. cameraCheck: Closed pressure cooker sitting off flame. Video shot: Turning off flame knob on stove. Timer: 600 seconds.

steps.title: Fluff and serve
steps.text: Open cooker lid, gently fluff rice from edges with a flat spatula, and transfer to a serving plate.
steps.visualCue: Individual tiny rice grains are tender, separate, glossy, and fragrant with chicken cooked soft.
steps.watchOut: Vigorous stirring breaks fragile Seeraga Samba grains; lift gently from sides. cameraCheck: Fluffed biryani with visible chicken pieces and tiny distinct grains. Video shot: Spatula gently fluffing hot biryani in cooker.
